newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST-Italy April new car sales seen up sharply.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Italy April new car sales seen up sharply.

text.p: Italian new car registrations in April should show a sharp rise of around 25 to 30 percent year-on-year as the domestic market continues to pick up, auto sector analysts and sources said.
Registrations in April 1996 totalled 151,905. In March this year they jumped 25.04 percent to 220,500, boosted by the government's car buying incentive scheme introduced in January.

"If we take into account a rise of 25 percent, which in this case seems normal, and consider that April this year had one more working day than in April last year which equals some 10,000 vehicles, then we look like seeing a total of around the 200,000 level," said Gian Paolo Trasi of Imi Sigeco. No-one was available for comment at market leader Fiat.
The Transport Ministry is due to issue official April new registrations data either on the afternoon of Friday May 9 or on the morning of Saturday May 10.
"March this year was the first month to show real effects (of the scheme). But we could see a higher level in April as we are in a phase of acceleration," said Giuliana Porta at brokers AFV Sim.

"March and April are still benefiting from the large flows of orders seen since the start of the year. Now we need to see whether we can keep up the same rhythm over the months to come," said one analyst who preferred not to be named.
